newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil sold down on lower IPE.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil sold down on lower IPE.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps was sold down late afternoon on Wednesday on a sharply weaker gas oil futures market in London, market sources said.
The market was already traded down this morning on lower overnight crude values following the release of bearish American Petroleum Institute (API) figures, they said.

January gas oil swaps traded this afternoon to a low of $30.60 a barrel from this morning traded levels of between $30.95-$31.10 a barrel, brokers said. The market was last quoted at $30.50/$30.60 a barrel, down about $1.00 from Tuesday's values, they said.
January gas oil futures was last traded at 0940 GMT at $209.00 a tonne, down $5.75 from its Tuesday close.

The big fall to crude prices were due to API figures showed that crude oil stocks rose 324,000 barrels, distillates stocks climbed by over two million barrels and gasoline were up by almost six million barrels.
Jet fuel prices also fell with the gas oil market but the jet fuel/gas oil swap spread or regrade was steady.
Brokers said January regrade was last quoted at $2.00/$2.40 a barrel, just above the $2.00 traded mark in Tuesday evening.
Fuel oil edged up slightly despite the weaker crude market with support seen from regional buying interest.
January swaps was last quoted at $119.25/$120.00 per tonne, up about 50 cents from Tuesday.

Naphtha prices were offered down, sharply lower in line with the crude market but buyers were sidelined with January swaps offered at $24.20 a barrel compared to Tuesday's offer price of $25.05, one broker said.
